newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported by fresh buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported by fresh buying interest.

text.p: Fresh physical demand emerged to support the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Friday, but traders did not expect major gains in the near term.
A local trader, who bought at least five cargoes in the past two weeks, started bidding on Thursday and bought a 180-cst cargo at $101.50 per tonne on Friday from a major, traders said.
Although the level was lower than the trader's previous buying level at $103.50 a week ago, the trade placed bullish sentiment in the market.
"Apparantly he is not bidding up the market but he does have buying interest," said one trader.
"So prices should be supported but there should not be major changes," he added.
A fire and explosion at the northern Taoyuan refinery of Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) on Thursday has yet caused any impact on the fuel oil market, traders said.
The late-afternoon blaze struck one of the refinery's two hydro-desulfurisation units, which were closed for annual maintenance, and was extinguished within an hour.
"We have to wait and see whether CPC will buy more cargoes next week. But so far the fire hasn't caused major impact," said one trader.

CPC issued earlier this week a tender to buy two 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil cargoes for July deliveries on a cost-and-freight basis (c-and-f) basis. The tender will close next Wednesday and is valid for two days.
"The fire should not affect our import plan because the units have been shut down for maintenance anyway," a CPC source said.
The fuel oil swaps market edged higher amid buying support from the local trader.
June swaps inched up to $101.00/$101.50 from $99.75/$100.25 and July were up to $100.00/$100.75 against $98.25/$99.75.
The low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market focused on a tender by the Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO) to buy one 500,000-barrel cargo for July delivery.
The tender, which closes on June 5 and is valid for one day, should provide some direction for the market, traders said.
